verses.1: To You, O LORD, I call, my God. Do not be silent to me, lest You be silent to me and I become like those who descend into the pit.
verses.2: Hear the voice of my plea when I call to You, when I raise my hands to the sanctuary of Your presence.
verses.3: Do not drag me away with the wicked, nor count me among evildoers. Those who speak peace to their neighbors, yet harbor evil in their hearts—
verses.4: give them according to their works, and according to the wickedness of their deeds. According to the work of their hands, give them; repay them for what they have done.
verses.5: For they do not understand the works of the LORD, nor the deeds of His hands. He will tear them down, and they will not be rebuilt.
verses.6: Praise be to the LORD, for He has heard the voice of my plea.
verses.7: The LORD is my strength and my shield. In Him my heart trusted and I was helped. My heart was lifted up, and I will sing praises to Him.
verses.8: The LORD is the strength of His people, the fortress of His salvation, His anointed.
verses.9: Save Your people and bless Your inheritance; tend them and lift them up forever.

notes:
Notes
- v. 3: "Those who speak peace to their neighbors, yet harbor evil in their hearts" — the phrase "רָעָה בִּלְבָבָם" is rendered as "harbor evil in their hearts" to maintain the contrast with outwardly peaceful speech.
- v. 8: "His anointed" — "מְשִׁיחוֹ" is rendered as a possessive form ("His anointed"), not as a title. The context does not suggest a specific reference to a messianic figure.
raw:
[1] To You, O LORD, I call, my God. Do not be silent to me, lest You be silent to me and I become like those who descend into the pit.

[2] Hear the voice of my plea when I call to You, when I raise my hands to the sanctuary of Your presence.

[3] Do not drag me away with the wicked, nor count me among evildoers. Those who speak peace to their neighbors, yet harbor evil in their hearts—

[4] give them according to their works, and according to the wickedness of their deeds. According to the work of their hands, give them; repay them for what they have done.

[5] For they do not understand the works of the LORD, nor the deeds of His hands. He will tear them down, and they will not be rebuilt.

[6] Praise be to the LORD, for He has heard the voice of my plea.

[7] The LORD is my strength and my shield. In Him my heart trusted and I was helped. My heart was lifted up, and I will sing praises to Him.

[8] The LORD is the strength of His people, the fortress of His salvation, His anointed.

[9] Save Your people and bless Your inheritance; tend them and lift them up forever.

---
Notes
- v. 3: "Those who speak peace to their neighbors, yet harbor evil in their hearts" — the phrase "רָעָה בִּלְבָבָם" is rendered as "harbor evil in their hearts" to maintain the contrast with outwardly peaceful speech.
- v. 8: "His anointed" — "מְשִׁיחוֹ" is rendered as a possessive form ("His anointed"), not as a title. The context does not suggest a specific reference to a messianic figure.
